reading.body:
CyrusOne's Houston campus is the largest data center in Texas by published IT load, at 84 MW across HOU3 and HOU4, which is 18 percent of the 475 MW that Texas facilities disclose.

That ranking measures disclosure as much as capacity. Texas has 133 mapped data centers and only 19 publish power figures, so the state total of 475 MW is a floor, not a sum. The 84 MW is still a concrete quantity: at 40 kW per rack it is roughly 2,100 racks, and at 10 kW per GPU it is roughly 8,400 high-end accelerators if the whole load went to GPU compute.

For AI scaling, that is enough capacity to matter at the state level and not enough to settle anything nationally. The campus holds 347,000 square feet of technical space and a Green Globes certification, which speaks to energy efficiency operations rather than AI workload suitability. Nothing published states whether the site's grid connection can support sustained training loads, and the grid is where the constraint sits.

What the data does not cover is the rest of Texas. The other 114 mapped facilities publish no power figures, so this campus's true share of AI-ready supply in the state cannot be calculated. No announced expansion is recorded, and the suitability score of 77 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
